findings.title: Options-object construction enables rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: The options destructuring path uses `rejectOnClear = true`, so `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` flips on rejection even though the documented and typed default is false.
findings.impact: Callers that follow the documented options-object form can get unexpected `AbortError` rejections from `clearQueue()`, which changes teardown and `Promise.all` behavior instead of leaving discarded work unresolved.
findings.evidence: Code: `index.js:6-13`. Contract: `readme.md:46-58`, `index.d.ts:99-106`. Probe: `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` + `clearQueue()` rejected a pending promise with `AbortError`, while `pLimit(1)` left the comparable pending promise unsettled.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run a `node --input-type=module` probe that enqueues one running task and one pending task with `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); await pending;` and observe `{"name":"AbortError","message":"This operation was aborted"}`.

findings.title: limitFunction drops all call arguments to the wrapped function
findings.cause: The wrapper returned from `limitFunction()` is `() => limit(() => function_())`, so it never forwards the caller's arguments into `function_`.
findings.impact: Reusable limited functions that accept parameters silently receive `undefined` inputs. That breaks the documented `limitFunction()` use case and the `recipes.md` example that wraps `fetchUrl(url)`.
findings.evidence: Code: `index.js:121-124`. Contract: `index.d.ts:133-136`, `recipes.md:142-163`. Probe: wrapping `async (a, b) => ({a: String(a), b: String(b)})` and calling `limited('left', 'right')` returned `{"a":"undefined","b":"undefined"}`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `const limited = limitFunction(async (a, b) => ({a: String(a), b: String(b)}), {concurrency: 1}); console.log(await limited('left', 'right'));` and observe both arguments arrive as `undefined`.

findings.title: limit.map omits mapper index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper call site passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`, so Sets, iterators, and other iterables never receive the documented index argument.
findings.impact: Code that relies on `limit.map()` to supply stable indexes across general iterables breaks silently for `Set` and iterator inputs even though the README and typings promise `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => ...)` semantics.
findings.evidence: Code: `index.js:107-112`. Contract: `readme.md:78-85`, `index.d.ts:30-43`. Probe: `await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b', 'c']), async (value, index) => ...)` recorded indexes as `undefined` for every item.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run a `node --input-type=module` probe with `const seen = []; await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b', 'c']), async (value, index) => { seen.push({value, index: String(index)}); }); console.log(seen);` and observe every `index` string is `"undefined"`.

findings.title: rejectOnClear validation accepts falsey non-boolean values
findings.cause: The type guard checks `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`, which only rejects truthy non-booleans and lets `0`, `''`, and `null` slip through.
findings.impact: Misconfigured callers do not get a `TypeError` for invalid option values and instead silently fall back to falsey behavior, making API misuse harder to detect.
findings.evidence: Code: `index.js:12-13`. Contract: `readme.md:46-52`, `index.d.ts:99-106`. Probe: `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})`, `''`, and `null` all constructed successfully instead of throwing.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `for (const value of [0, '', null]) { try { pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: value}); console.log('accepted'); } catch { console.log('rejected'); } }` and observe all three invalid values are accepted.
